description: The bar chart titled “Average Entropy Across Sycophancy Reduction Methods on Static Experiments” illustrates the comparative performance of three sycophancy reduction methods — Baseline (pink), Source Info (beige), and Direct Command (light blue) — across three different AI models: GPT-4, Claude, and Llama. The vertical axis, labeled “Entropy Average Values,” ranges from 3.0 to 6.0 in increments of 0.5, representing the average entropy scores associated with each method-model combination. For GPT-4, the Baseline method yields an entropy of approximately 4.9, Source Info reaches about 5.25, and Direct Command is slightly lower at roughly 5.05. In Claude, the Baseline entropy is around 4.7, Source Info peaks at approximately 5.15, and Direct Command is about 4.95. For Llama, the Baseline drops to approximately 4.55, Source Info is around 4.95, and Direct Command is approximately 4.8. Across all models, Source Info consistently produces the highest entropy values, followed by Direct Command and then Baseline, suggesting that Source Info introduces the most uncertainty or diversity in responses under static experimental conditions. The bars are grouped by model along the horizontal axis, with each group containing three adjacent bars corresponding to the three methods, and the legend in the upper right corner clarifies the color coding. The chart does not indicate error bars or statistical significance, focusing purely on mean entropy values.
